antidotes.why: Find the friend; trees that stand together hold each other up.
Surrender is the companion of those who have no one.
Remembering is a kind of nearness.

chains.summary: Alone, he was afraid. He reflected that since there is nothing other than him, he has nothing to fear. The fear left. Fear comes only from a second. Alone, he also found no joy, and one who is alone does not rejoice.
chains.title: Fear comes from a second

verses.m: He was afraid; that is why one who is alone is afraid. Then he thought: 'Since there is nothing but me, what am I afraid of?' At that his fear left him. What was there to fear? Fear arises only from a second.
verses.sa: सोऽबिभेत् तस्मादेकाकी बिभेति । स हायमीक्षां चक्रे यन्मदन्यन्नास्ति कस्मान्नु बिभेमीति । तत एवास्य भयं वीयाय । कस्माद्ध्यभेष्यत् द्वितीयाद्वै भयं भवति ॥

depicts.m: Where one's beloved is, even the foot of a tree is home. Without her, even a palace is a wilderness.
depicts.sa: वृक्षमूलेऽपि दयिता यस्य तिष्ठति तद्गृहम् / प्रासादोपि तया हीनः कान्तार इति निश्चितम्
depicts.why: Spoken by the pigeon waiting through a storm for a mate who has not come home.

depicts.m: Friend, I am mad with love, and no one knows my pain. Only the wounded know what the wounded go through, only one who has been wounded.
depicts.r: Meera pada "Mero darad na jane koy"
depicts.sa: हे री मैं तो प्रेम-दिवानी मेरो दरद न जाणै कोय। घायल की गति घायल जाणै, जो कोई घायल होय।
depicts.why: Depicts pain no one around her understands.

depicts.m: He was known as supremely detached, yet on seeing Sita his composure fled. The king held Janaki to his heart, and the great banks of his wisdom gave way.
depicts.sa: सीय बिलोकि धीरता भागी। रहे कहावत परम बिरागी॥ लीन्हि रायँ उर लाइ जानकी। मिटी महामरजाद ग्यान की ॥
depicts.why: Holds her to his heart knowing she is leaving.

depicts.m: Somewhere he taught knowledge to sages, somewhere he told of Ram's virtues. Though free of all desire, the wise Lord was pained by separation from his devotee.
depicts.sa: कतहुँ मुनिन्ह उपदेसहिं ग्याना। कतहुँ राम गुन करहिं बखाना॥ जदपि अकाम तदपि भगवाना। भगत बिरह दुख दुखित सुजाना ॥
depicts.why: Shows him wandering, teaching and singing, carrying her absence.

depicts.m: May all the gods and ancestors guard you, my lord, the way eyelids guard the eyes. The term of your exile is the water, and your loved ones are the fish in it; you are kind and steadfast in what is right.
depicts.sa: देव पितर सब तुम्हहि गोसाईं। राखहुँ पलक नयन की नाईं॥ अवधि अंबु प्रिय परिजन मीना। तुम्ह करुनाकर धरम धुरीना ॥
depicts.why: Depicts the fish left behind and the years of exile as water.

depicts.m: Stay well, mother Yashoda. In four or five days we two brothers will come. Since the day I was parted from you, no one has called me "Kanhaiya". I have not had breakfast in the morning, nor warm milk at evening.
depicts.sa: नीके रहियो जसुमति मैया। आवैंगे दिन चारि पाँच में हम हलधर दोउ भैया॥ जा दिन तें हम तुमतें बिछुरे काहु न कह्यो 'कन्हैया'। कबहूँ प्रात न कियो कलेवा, साँझ न पीन्हीं धैया॥
depicts.why: Shows no one uses the name only home used.

depicts.m: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
depicts.sa: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥
depicts.why: Tears have not stopped since he left.

depicts.m: The mother gazes at his little bow and arrows. Again and again she presses the Lord's small, lovely shoes to her heart and eyes. Sometimes, as before, she goes to wake him with tender words: "Get up, my child, your mother adores your face; your brothers and friends are all at the door."
depicts.sa: जननी निरखति बान-धनुहियाँ। बार-बार उर नैननि लावति प्रभुजूकी ललित पनहियाँ॥ कबहुँ प्रथम ज्यों जाइ जगावति कहि प्रिय बचन सँवारे। उठहु तात! बलि मातु बदनपर, अनुज-सखा सब द्वारे॥

gloss: The ache of being apart from someone, home or God. The Upanishad says the first being, alone, found no joy; the epics give it to Rama, Sita and the gopis.

heals.m: I am the goal, the sustainer, the master, the witness, the home, the refuge and the friend; the origin and the dissolution, the ground, the treasure-house and the undying seed.
heals.sa: गतिर्भर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी निवासः शरणं सुहृत् । प्रभवः प्रलयः स्थानं निधानं बीजमव्ययम् ॥
heals.why: Shows the speaker as home, shelter and friend.

heals.m: The Lord is the companion of exactly those who have no one: kind to the lowly, supremely compassionate, Hari who takes many forms for the good of his people.
heals.sa: नाथ अनाथनि ही के संगी। दीनदयाल, परम करुनामय, जन-हित हरि बहु-रंगी ॥
heals.why: Having no one is the very condition he keeps company with.

heals.m: One God is hidden in all beings: all-pervading, the inner self of every being, overseer of all action, dwelling in all beings, the witness, pure awareness, alone, beyond all qualities.
heals.sa: एको देवः सर्वभूतेषु गूढः सर्वव्यापी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा। कर्माध्यक्षः सर्वभूताधिवासः साक्षी चेता केवलो निर्गुणश्च ॥
heals.why: Shows no one is ever unaccompanied, the same one dwells in each.

heals.m: Rahim says: remembering is best of all, when it comes again and again. People who were separated meet again; know that this is why God takes birth.
heals.sa: रहिमन सुधि सबते भली, लगै जो बारम्बार। बिछुरे मानुष फिरि मिलैं, यहै जानि अवतार॥
heals.why: Shows remembering keeps the parted close.

heals.m: Tulsi, tell the kind Ram all of it, your good points and your faults. Your misery will grow thin and your contentment will grow full.
heals.sa: तुलसी राम कृपालु सों कहि सुनाउ गुन दोष। होय दूबरी दीनता परम पीन संतोष॥

heals.m: Listen once more, mighty-armed, to my supreme word, which I will speak for your good, because you delight in it and are dear to me.
heals.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचभूय एव महाबाहो श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । यत्तेऽहं प्रीयमाणाय वक्ष्यामि हितकाम्यया ॥
heals.why: Shows someone wishes your good and says so.

heals.m: Hear once more my highest word, the most secret of all: you are deeply loved by me, and so I will tell you what is good for you.
heals.sa: सर्वगुह्यतमं भूयः श्रृणु मे परमं वचः । इष्टोऽसि मे दृढमिति ततो वक्ष्यामि ते हितम् ॥

heals.m: Learning is a person's greater beauty, a hidden and guarded treasure. Learning brings enjoyment, fame and happiness; it is the teacher of teachers. In a foreign land learning is your kin; learning is the highest deity. Kings honour learning, not wealth. Without learning a person is little more than an animal.
heals.sa: विद्या नाम नरस्य रूपमधिकं प्रच्छन्नगुप्तं धनं विद्या भोगकरी यशस्सुखकरी विद्या गुरूणां गुरुः । विद्या बन्धुजनो विदेशगमने विद्या परा देवता विद्या राजसु पूजिता न तु धनं विद्याविहीनः पशुः ॥
heals.why: Far from home, what one knows keeps one company.

hero.m: Night and day our eyes keep raining. Ever since Shyam went away, it is always the rainy season for us.
hero.sa: निसिदिन बरसत नैन हमारे। सदा रहति पावस ऋतु हम पै जब तें स्याम सिधारे॥

loci.m: Show me your great-hearted kindness, best of men. I have you, my protector, and yet I look like someone who has no one.
loci.sa: स कुरुष्व महोत्साहां कृपां मयि नरर्षभ। त्वया नाथवती नाथ अनाथा इव दृश्यते॥

practices.m: Friend mind, what is the use of so much chatter? Friend mind, all this is mere speculation. I have told you the heart of it: you are reality itself, vast as the sky.
practices.sa: सखे मनः किं बहुजल्पितेन सखे मनः सर्वमिदं वितर्क्यम् । यत्सारभूतं कथितं मया ते त्वमेव तत्त्वं गगनोपमोऽसि ॥

practices.m: Whoever offers me with devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, that offering of love from the pure-hearted I accept.
practices.sa: पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः ॥
practices.why: Shows devotion as what makes the gift.

practices.m: Wealth has three destinies: giving, enjoying and loss. Whoever neither gives nor enjoys it meets the third.
practices.sa: दानं भोगो नाशस्तिस्रो गतयो भवन्ति वित्तस्य । यो न ददाति न भुङ्क्ते तस्य तृतीया गतिर्भवति ॥

practices.m: Giving in secret, a warm welcome for whoever comes home, silence after doing a kindness, speaking in public of kindness received, no arrogance in wealth, talking of others without a whiff of contempt: who taught the good this vow, hard as walking a sword's edge?
practices.sa: प्रदानं प्रच्छन्नं गृहमुपगते सम्भ्रमविधिः प्रियं कृत्वा मौनं सदसि कथनं चाप्युपकृते । अनुत्सेको लक्ष्म्यामनभिभवगन्धाः परकथाः सतां केनोद्दिष्टं विषममसिधाराव्रतमिदम् ॥

practices.m: The ear is beautiful through learning, not earrings; the hand through giving, not bracelets; the body of the compassionate shines through helping others, not through sandal paste.
practices.sa: श्रोत्रं श्रुतेनैव न कुण्डलेन दानेन पाणिर्न तु कङ्कणेन । विभाति कायः करुणापराणां परोपकारैर्न तु चन्दनेन ॥
practices.why: Shows the body shining by helping.

practices.m: Ocean of compassion, Ganapati: may your radiance, which the whole world worships, by its own power quickly guard our minds, day and night, from wrong action, and urge them to good action. Blessed one, with Siddhi at your left side, we bow to you.
practices.sa: भर्गो विश्वसमर्चितं यदिह ते ह्यास्ते दयासागर ! तन्नो बुद्धिमहर्निशं गणपते ! शक्तचा स्वया सत्वरम । संरक्ष्यासत एव कर्मनिवहात् सत्कर्मणि प्रेरयेत् सियाऽलङ्कृतवामपार्श्व ! भगवस्त्वां सन्नमामो वयमा ॥

practices.m: Provisions for the wilderness of life, medicine that cuts the bonds of the world, rescue from sorrow and grief: the two syllables 'Ha-ri'.
Madhava is the father and the mother of all beings. Go to him for refuge, best of the Kurus; he is the refuge.
practices.sa: सर्वेषामेव भूतानां पिता माता च माधवः / गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं शरण्यं कौरवर्षभाः

stories.l: When everything you knew is underwater, you have not been forgotten; you are being held.
stories.s: At the end of an age, the sage Markandeya drifts alone over a flooded world and sees a radiant child on a banyan branch. The child draws him inside his body, where he sees all the worlds, then asks if he has been resting, tired. Narayana explains he showed himself because he saw Markandeya's distress. Markandeya tells the Pandavas that this child is Krishna, sitting with them.
stories.t: Markandeya and the child on the banyan leaf

stories.l: Compulsions can take everything. Loyalty and patience can still bring you home.
stories.s: King Nala, possessed by the spirit Kali, gambles away his kingdom to his brother and abandons Damayanti in the forest. Years of separation and disguise follow, until Nala masters the dice and the two are reunited.

stories.l: Letting go of an expectation can bring the sleep that waiting never will.
stories.s: Pingala waited all night for a lover who never came. At last she saw that her peace depended on someone else's arrival, let the expectation go, and slept peacefully.
stories.t: Pingala's song: the night she stopped waiting

stories.l: Friendships made in hard times deserve to be kept; say so out loud.
stories.s: After six happy months, Ram sends his monkey and bear friends home with gifts. Angad, whose father is dead, begs to stay: Ram is his father and mother now. Ram embraces him and sends him on. To the boatman Guha he says: you are a brother to me; keep visiting.
stories.t: Ram says goodbye to his friends
